doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Symphonic challenges: Villa-Lobos and 'The Rite of Spring'
summary: Raph mentions recording 'Forest of the Amazon' with Villa-Lobos and playing bass trumpet in 'The Rite of Spring' with the Ridgefield Symphony.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: How about classical experiences? Are there any particular pieces — Stravinsky or anything like that — you’ve ever had really challenging work in the symphonic world?
Yeah. I recorded “Forest of the Amazon” with Villa Lobos and that had some moments. And there are a number of symphonic things. Yeah. There were moments, a lot of moments.
I got to watch the Nashville Symphony rehearse “The Rite of Spring” once, and I was watching the score and I just couldn’t understand how can you play this?

You know, I did it last year with a local symphony, the Ridgefield Symphony. I played bass trumpet. And it was the first time I ever played bass trumpet on “The Rite of Spring.” And the bass trumpet does not play much, but when it plays it’s out there, you hear it. And it took some counting and it took a little bit of paying attention. And it came off but I didn’t just toss it off as well here’s something else to do. I was on the edge of my chair more than the back of the chair.
